newsitem.title: USA: Dole says U.S. must be decisive and humble Saddam.
newsitem.headline: Dole says U.S. must be decisive and humble Saddam.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole said on Tuesday he hoped President Bill Clinton's missile strike against Iraq marked the start of decisive action to humble Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein.

Dole, a Second World War veteran whose war wounds left him with a useless right arm, told an American Legion convention that the entire history of the 20th Century was a warning against appeasing "butchers" like Saddam.

"If there is one clear lesson of our century it is this: When aggression is tolerated it multiplies. And I trust this is the beginning of decisive action to limit the power and arrogance of Saddam Hussein," Dole said.

"He (Saddam) has persecuted his people, he has defied the international community time and time again, and tested the resolve of America. And we must be decisive in confronting this threat and humbling this tyrant," Dole said.
The Republican presidential hopeful was applauded enthusiastically by some 6,000 veterans in the audience, many of them elderly men wearing medals and ribbons.

Over the weekend Dole had blamed the latest flareup In Iraq on a failure of Clinton's leadership in dealing with Saddam, but the Republican candidate avoided any direct criticism while speaking to the veterans on Tuesday.
He said he had had the "privilege" of speaking with Clinton by telephone on Tuesday about the U.S. action in Iraq, as well as with Colin Powell, former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
"The bottom line is that Saddam Hussein is an outlaw, he's a tryant, he's a butcher, and we cannot tolerate any (additional) action by him in that part of the world," Dole declared.

The Republican said his thoughts and prayers were with U.S. men and women involved in the military action against Iraq. "They are freedom's heroes and we support them without hesitation or reservation," he said.

Repeating some comments he made earlier on Tuesday in a written statement, Dole said the goal of the U.S. action should be the withdrawal of Saddam's troops from the Kurdish-populated north of Iraq, the release of Kurdish prisoners, and a halt to interference by both Iraq and Iran among the Kurds.
In addition, he said the action should be aimed at reestablishing U.N. weapons inspection efforts "and an end to Saddam's support of international terrorism."
Dole, in remarks over the weekend, had accused Clinton of unwisely accepting the planned relaxation of sanctions on Iraqi oil sales.
He also had accused Clinton of doing little recently to protest Saddam's continued obstruction of nuclear weapons inspectors except to "join in weak statements by the U.N. Security Council."
